newsitem.title: INDIA: India's lower house to vote on Finance Bill.
newsitem.headline: India's lower house to vote on Finance Bill.

text.p: India's lower house of parliament, the Lok Sabha, is expected to approve Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's landmark 1997/98 (April-March) budget on Friday, government officials said.
"The Finance Bill for 1997/98 will be voted and approved by the Lok Sabha on Friday after Chidambaram replies to the two-day discussion on it," a Finance Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.
Chidambaram was scheduled to speak on the floor of the Lok Sabha in the early afternoon. It was not known whether he would offer any changes in the bill.
On Wednesday, he announced some minor tax and tariff concessions which would cost the exchequer 1.1 billion rupees this fiscal year.
The Finance Bill, which contains the tax and tariff proposals of the 1997/98 budget plan, will be taken up by the upper house, the Rajya Sabha, after its approval in the Lok Sahba.
The Rajya Sabha was expected to return the bill next week. It would then be sent to President Shankar Dayal Sharma for his signature.
